common_name: Teresa Autumn Sage (White-and-Purple Bicolor Salvia greggii)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; performs best with lean soil and minimal supplemental irrigation once established.

directions: Plant in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Teresa is a white-flowered branch sport of a red Salvia greggii, discovered by a Texas grower and named for his wife; the white flowers carry a light purple flush at the base above the calyx and purple streaks on the lower lip, giving the plant a subtly bicolor effect distinct from the pure-white 'Alba'. It forms an upright, deer-resistant clump topped with flowers in a strong spring flush, then sporadically through summer heat, before a second major bloom in fall. Cut back hard to 6-8 inches in late winter to keep growth dense and encourage maximum flower production the following season; hummingbirds are strongly drawn to the fall flush.

common_name: Flame Autumn Sage (Fragrant Dark-Red Salvia greggii)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; performs best with lean soil and minimal supplemental irrigation once established.

directions: Plant in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Flame is a small, semi-evergreen Salvia greggii selection bearing dark red flowers set off by contrasting purple calyces, produced heavily in spring and again in fall with lighter bloom through summer. Both the flowers and foliage carry a light fragrance, and the plant is a reliable draw for hummingbirds and butterflies. Cut back by about a third in late winter to maintain a tidy, well-branched shrub and to promote the strongest spring flush.

common_name: Purple Pastel Autumn Sage (Compact Purple-Flowered Salvia greggii)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; ensure sharp drainage, especially in regions with heavy summer rainfall.

directions: Plant in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Purple Pastel is a small, tidy Salvia greggii selection forming a compact clump topped heavily with purple flowers in spring and fall and more sporadically through summer heat. Its low, dense habit suits border edges, rock gardens, and small-space plantings where taller autumn sage cultivars would overwhelm the design. Sharp drainage is essential, particularly in humid climates prone to heavy summer rain. Cut back lightly after each bloom flush to keep the mound neat and encourage continued flowering.

common_name: San Carlos Festival Baby Sage (Floriferous Red-Violet Salvia microphylla)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in late summer or set out container plants in spring, in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; this selection was discovered in the village of San Carlos in Tamaulipas, Mexico, and introduced to cultivation by Yucca Do Nursery.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to light afternoon shade in hot climates. San Carlos Festival forms a compact, wide-spreading mound and is among the most floriferous Salvia microphylla selections, producing dense red-violet, two-lipped flowers continuously from early May through November. Its low, broad habit makes it well suited to border fronts and mass plantings where a long season of color is wanted. Cut back hard in late winter to renew growth and maintain a dense, well-branched shape; established plants tolerate heat and drought with only occasional supplemental water.

common_name: Newby Hall Baby Sage (Blood-Red RHS Award-of-Merit Salvia microphylla)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in late summer or set out container plants in spring, in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; this cultivar holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to light afternoon shade in hot climates. Newby Hall is a bushy Salvia microphylla selection with yellowish-green ovate leaves and blood-red, two-lipped flowers about an inch long produced in late summer and autumn, holding the RHS Award of Garden Merit for reliable garden performance. Cut back hard to 6-12 inches in late winter to renew growth and keep the shrub dense; once established it tolerates heat and drought well, needing supplemental water only during extended dry spells.

common_name: Kew Red Baby Sage (RHS Award-of-Merit Red Salvia microphylla)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in late summer or set out container plants in spring, in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; this cultivar holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to light afternoon shade in hot climates. Kew Red is a compact, woody-based Salvia microphylla selection producing abundant true-red, two-lipped flowers from summer through fall, and holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for consistent garden performance. Cut back hard to 6-12 inches in late winter to renew growth and maintain a dense mound; established plants are heat- and drought-tolerant, needing supplemental water only in extended dry spells, and draw hummingbirds throughout the bloom season.

common_name: Pink Blush Baby Sage (RHS Award-of-Merit Pink Salvia microphylla)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in late summer or set out container plants in spring, in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; this cultivar holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to light afternoon shade in hot climates. Pink Blush is a compact, woody-based Salvia microphylla selection bearing soft pink, two-lipped flowers from summer through fall, and holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for reliable performance in the garden. Cut back hard to 6-12 inches in late winter to renew growth and keep the mound dense and floriferous; once established it tolerates heat and drought well and is a steady draw for hummingbirds.

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Trebah requires excellent drainage and lean to average soil to avoid floppy, short-lived growth.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Trebah is a Salvia x jamensis hybrid (Salvia greggii x Salvia microphylla) producing near-white, tubular flowers with just a flush of pinky lilac about the corolla tube and upper lip, blooming from spring to autumn on a compact, mounding shrub. Its soft, understated coloring pairs well with more saturated red and pink jamensis and greggii cultivars in mixed borders. Light trimming after each bloom flush encourages fresh growth and continued flowering; extraordinarily drought-tolerant once established and well suited to rock gardens and container culture.

common_name: Rockin' Blue Suede Shoes Salvia (Light Blue Black-Calyx Anise Sage)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts in spring once soil has warmed, in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; a Proven Winners selection that is sterile and does not set seed, so it blooms continuously all season.

directions: Rockin' Blue Suede Shoes is a compact, well-branched Salvia guaranitica selection bred for a more floriferous, self-cleaning habit than seed-grown anise sage, producing light blue flowers set off by contrasting black calyces from early summer through frost. Because it is sterile it puts no energy into seed production and instead blooms continuously without deadheading, making it one of the most reliable hummingbird plants for Gulf Coast gardens. Grown as a returning perennial in zones 9-10 and as a warm-season annual farther north; cut dieback to a few inches after hard frost and mulch the crown in marginal zones, as it can return from the roots even after top growth is lost.

Cut dieback to a few inches after hard frost and mulch the crown in marginal zones, as it can return from the roots even after top growth is lost.
